thread.title: JPMorgan Chase giving raises, adding 4,000 jobs, boosting small business lending from Trump tax cuts

author: Mike Sunnucks
title: JPMorgan Chase giving raises, adding 4,000 jobs, boosting small business lending from Trump tax cuts
text: – Senior Reporter, Phoenix Business Journal Jan 23, 2018, 8:15am MST JPMorgan Chase & Co, (NYSE: JPM) is giving employees raises and bonuses as part of a $20 billion, five-year U.S. investment effort. JPMorgan joins a chorus of other big and regional banks and other companies giving bonuses, raises and increasing investments after tax cuts passed by President Donald Trump and Congress. Chase said it will raise workers' pay from between $12 and $16.50 per hour to $15 and $18 per hour. In Arizona, more than 1,000 Chase employees will see their pay bumped up to $15 per hour, according to a JPMorgan spokesperson. Eight hundred of those workers are in metro Phoenix. Chase has a big operational footprint in downtown Phoenix and is building a big campus in Tempe. In more expensive markets such as New York, New Jersey and San Francisco will see base pay increase to $18 per hour. Workers in Chicago and Detroit will get raises to $16.50, the bank announced. The raises will benefit 22,000 Chase employees working at branches and customer service employees. They will also be getting a $750 bonus and Chase is cutting health insurance costs $750 per year for employees making less than $60,000. Chase joins Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), Wells Fargo (NYSE: WFC) and a number of other banks in offering bonuses or raises to employees after the Trump tax cuts were passed last month. JPMorgan also plans on hiring 4,000 new workers, will open new branches and upping small business lending by $4 billion. “Over 99 percent of American companies are small to mid-sized businesses and account for over half of the jobs created in the U.S. This important segment of the economy drives growth and is critical to the health of our communities” said Doug Petno, CEO of JPMorgan Commercial Banking. “Today, we support over 4 million small and mid-sized business clients, and we will be expanding our efforts and working even harder to deliver capital and ideas to support their success.” Chase will also open new offices in Bethesda, Maryland and Charleston, South Carolina and plans on hiring 500 new home lending advisors. Chase’s $20 billion plan comes after Apple Inc. (Nasdaq: AAPL) announced a $350 billion, five-year U.S. investment boost stemming from the tax cuts. – Senior Reporter, Phoenix Business Journal Jan 23, 2018, 8:15am MST
